page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-192 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 192 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) and 744.0 gigabytes (GB) of random-access memory (RAM). This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without any integrated graphics processing units (GPUs) and does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-standard-192 offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, aligning closely with general-purpose hardware profiles. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities for multi-threaded workloads. However, the absence of bundled local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses represents a structural tradeoff, requiring external network and storage provisioning which influences the overall deployment architecture and qualitative cost efficiency.

This server type is designed for large-scale workloads that require high parallel processing capacity without the need for hardware acceleration. Suitable applications include large-scale web serving, enterprise application hosting, distributed data processing, and general-purpose computational tasks that scale efficiently across 192 dedicated vCPUs.
